person: Beverly Shaw is a 72-year-old retired fourth-grade teacher in Roanoke, Virginia, who is using an AI tool for the first time and is afraid of being scammed after losing $800 through her payment app last spring. A letter from a company called a 'finder' says she has money waiting in Ohio and offers to collect it for a quarter of it, which sounds exactly like a scam to her. Her grandson Tyler set Athena up, and she wants each step explained and the chance to stop before anything is filed. She grew up as Beverly Hollis, married Walter Shaw in 1977, and was widowed in 2019. She lived in Dayton, Ohio until 1983, so she has old addresses and two names to check. She reads every screen twice and will not hurry.
stated_up_front: Hello, I'm sorry, I'm not very good with these things. I got a letter saying I might have money waiting in Ohio from years ago, and a company wants a share to collect it. Could you look and tell me what is real before anything is done? Please explain as you go.

facts.truth: Beverly Anne Hollis until she married in June 1977; Beverly Anne Shaw since then.
Dayton, Ohio (on Wyoming Street, 1977 to 1983, and with her parents before that); Roanoke, Virginia since August 1983, at the same house on Carlin Road since 1991.
A company called Lostfunds wrote on 2 October 2026, offering to recover a life insurance payout for 25 percent of it. She has not replied or signed.
A refund of $212.60 from a Dayton electric company, listed under Beverly Hollis at her parents' old address. Her mother's 1970s letters in the Binderwell folder show she lived there.
A life policy payout of $640.00 under Beverly A Shaw at the Wyoming Street address in Dayton. It is the policy the finder wants 25 percent of.
An uncashed school-district payroll check for $88.15 under Beverly A Shaw at Carlin Road, dated 2014.
A $389.00 listing under Walter J Shaw in Virginia. Walter died in March 2019, so it belongs to his estate and not to her to claim as her own.
A Beverly M Shaw in Richmond has a $1,150 listing. Beverly is sure it is not hers, because her middle name is Anne.
She knows the last four digits of her Social Security number and will give them only once she understands why. She will not give a full account number.
Her daughter Carol calls every Sunday and asks whether she has 'done anything about the bank'. Her grandson Tyler set up Athena.

unknowns: Whether a finder is allowed to charge 25 percent, and what limit Ohio or Virginia sets.
Whether the claim deadline matters, or how long a claim takes.
Whether Walter's listing needs probate papers or a different form, since she does not know how his estate was settled.
What 'holder' or 'reported property' means on the state sites.
